nodes.title: Nonregular lifting data
nodes.statement: A CG lifting datum consists of an odd prime p≥5, a finite extension E/Qp with integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k; an integer a with p−1>a≥2; a continuous absolutely irreducible odd residual representation r̄:GQ→GSp₄(k) with multiplier ε̄^(1−a); chosen nondegenerate roots α,β; and a local basis at p with diagonal λ(α),λ(β),ε̄^(1−a)λ(β⁻¹),ε̄^(1−a)λ(α⁻¹), zero (1,2) and (3,4) entries and an unramified isotropic two-plane. It also records CG20 Assumptions 4.1–4.3, the minimal local deformation conditions and a chosen nonzero cuspidal residual eigensystem. The generic deformation functors, representations and pairings are supplied objects, not new definitions here.
proofSteps: Use the supplier representation, pairing and deformation objects and impose this particular conjunction of conditions.

Keep three image conditions separate: Q(ad⁰r̄) excludes ζp; for every m there is σ∈GQ(ζpᵐ) with four distinct roots and eigenvalue 1 on each irreducible adjoint constituent; the images of ad⁰r̄ and ad⁰r̄(1) have no quotient of order p.

Record away-p types U₁,U₂,U₃ by unipotent monodromy ranks 1,2,3; P by two isotropic inertia-character planes with x−1 prime to p; H by absolutely irreducible inertia with x⁴−1 prime to p. Under the fixed cyclotomic multiplier the P case is empty.

The local minimal functor fixes the full multiplier, preserves those inertia conditions and, at p, has the split unramified two-plane with characters lifting the specified roots, as in Definition 4.6. Representability remains a supplier obligation.
acceptance: Do not replace Assumption 4.1 by adequacy, or the selected ordinary plane by an arbitrary filtration.
The multiplier is ε^(1−a), with ε of Hodge–Tate weight −1 and geometric Frobenius ε(Frobℓ)=ℓ⁻¹.

nodes.title: Minimal tame levels and the neat auxiliary prime
nodes.statement: From a CG lifting datum satisfying Assumption 4.2 choose q≥3, q∉S(r̄)∪{p}, with q≠1 mod p and no ratio of residual Frobenius eigenvalues equal to q. At U₁,U₂,U₃ primes choose respectively paramodular, Klingen and Iwahori level; at P choose strict Klingen level; at H choose full congruence level at x; impose full level q and hyperspecial level elsewhere. For Q disjoint from S(r̄)∪{p,q}, form K₀(Q), K₁(Q), their Klingen quotient ΔQ=∏x∈Q(Fx×)(p), and the intermediate cover XΔ(Q) for any quotient Δ of ΔQ. The prime q makes these moduli problems neat.
proofSteps: Choose the Frobenius class by Chebotarev from the stated neatness witness, then choose a prime outside the finite excluded set.
Use the suppliers for integral models, compatible fans and bundles; specify the local compact subgroups and their Klingen-character kernels.

nodes.title: No Steinberg component in scalar weight two
nodes.statement: If π is the cuspidal automorphic representation of a classical Siegel form of weight (2,2), then no finite local component is Steinberg in the source’s normalized central-character convention. At a Steinberg place x, the normalized Ux,1 eigenvalue in weight (j,k) is x^((j+k−6)/2), and in weight (2,2) it is x⁻¹, contradicting integrality of the Fourier-normalized Hecke action. Include any allowed finite unramified unit twist in the local calculation; its valuation does not change the contradiction.
proofSteps: Request the local Steinberg parameter and its U-eigenvalue in the exact geometric normalization from the GSp₄ local representation supplier.
Establish integrality of the action on the Fourier lattice and hence integrality of its eigenvalue.
At the residue characteristic x the proposed Steinberg eigenvalue has negative valuation; conclude it cannot occur.
acceptance: The proof is an integral Hecke-eigenvalue obstruction, not a consequence of an unproved association of an abelian variety to every weight-two form.

nodes.title: All-degree characteristic-zero interpolation
nodes.statement: For the characteristic-zero coherent eigensystems of NR2, the away-p Hecke action factors continuously through the inverse limit of finite free integral Hecke images on cuspidal H⁰ at varying p-levels and finite sets of regular weights. The resulting continuous semisimple ρΘ,λ:GQ→GL₄(Q̄p) is unramified outside Np and satisfies det(1−XρΘ,λ(Frobℓ))=Θ(Qℓ(X)) at ℓ∤Np. This applies to every coherent degree and both canonical and subcanonical extensions. It does not identify the unusual integral models in Pilloni–Stroh with a chosen Kottwitz lattice.
proofSteps: Import the geometric interpolation input for the modified ample Hodge bundle: Hodge–Tate sections give a Hecke-stable cover, and Čech localization modulo pˢ reduces classes to sections.
Clear denominators with high powers, use positivity and Serre vanishing to lift regular-weight sections, and pass through the finite integral Hecke images.
Use duality for the other extension convention; reconstruct the semisimple representation from the continuous determinant and good-prime identities.
Record an independent lattice-comparison obligation before applying this theorem to a specific torsion integral lattice.
acceptance: Do not infer CG20 Lemma 6.9 for its torsion lattice solely from this characteristic-zero theorem.

nodes.title: Central characters and residual Galois systems
